newsitem.title: NAMIBIA: NAMIBIA STOCKS WEEK - FOREIGN-OWNED FIRMS DOMINATE.
newsitem.headline: NAMIBIA STOCKS WEEK - FOREIGN-OWNED FIRMS DOMINATE.

text.p: Trading on the Namibian Stock Exchange (NSE) last week was dominated by foreign companies with large interests in Namibia as the local index ticked up, bourse officials said.

Through strong local buying De Beers traded a total of 50,200 shares worth N$ 8.3 million. About 132,000 Forbes shares changed hands, while Mutual and Federal traded 53,100 shares with the price down to N$ 27.75 from N$28.00.
Namibia Breweries finally started to recover with low volumes of just 8,400 shares traded, but the share price jumped back up to N$ 3.19 on Friday from N$ 2.95 at the start of the week.
As fishing firms moved lower, Namibian Sea Products ended the week on a further low, with prices down to 50 cents a share from 68 last week with 18,400 shares traded.
Officials said a total of 339,100 shares worth N$ 11.6 million were traded in the week.
The NSE overall index stood at 271.35 from 270.73 last week, while the NSE local index finished at 164.63 from 164.78 previously.
Meanwhile the company Profurn is to dual-list on the NSE on August 6, 1997.
